title: Reporting Verbs: How It Was Said

sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know *decir que* and the tense shifts of reported speech from B1 Unit 13 and B2 Unit 17. You also know a few reporting verbs: *afirmar* and *declarar* from B1 Unit 13, *asegurar* from B1 Unit 33, *advertir* and *sugerir* from B1 Unit 38, and *negar* and *desmentir* from B2 Unit 5. A reporting verb does more than say that someone spoke. It also says how the thing was said: firmly, as an admission, as a warning, as a blame. This lesson gives you the set of verbs and the rule for the mood that follows them. The next four lessons practise one group each.

sections.title: Ten verbs and what they add
rows: states it firmly, as something true
gives the reason or the way
warns, or draws attention to a danger
blames someone for what they did or did not do

sections.title: One rule for the mood
sections.content:
After a reporting verb, ask what follows it:

• **A fact the speaker states: indicative.** *Afirmó que la tienda cerraba a las ocho. Admitió que se había equivocado.* After a past verb the tense moves back, as in B2 Unit 17.
• **A claim that is rejected: subjunctive.** *Negó que fuera su error.* You know *negar que* + subjunctive from B2 Unit 5.
• ***Advertir* and *recordar* can report either.** If what follows is a fact, use the indicative: *Me advirtió que el tren salía a las ocho. Me recordó que la reunión era el lunes.* If it is something to do or not to do, use the subjunctive, as for the orders of B1 Unit 38: *Me advirtió que no llegara tarde. Me recordó que cerrara la puerta.*
• ***Sugerir* and *reprochar* take the subjunctive.** *Sugirió que esperáramos* (a proposal). *Me reprochó que no hubiera llamado* (a blame). For something that was not done, the pluperfect subjunctive is the form you learned in B2 Unit 16.

items.spanish: Afirmó que la tienda cerraba a las ocho.
items.english: He stated that the shop closed at eight.
She explained that she had no time.

items.spanish: Añadió que volvería al día siguiente.
items.english: He added that he would come back the next day.
She admitted that she had made a mistake.
He denied that it was his mistake.

items.spanish: Me advirtió que el tren salía a las ocho.
items.english: He warned me that the train left at eight.

items.spanish: Me advirtió que no llegara tarde.
items.english: He warned me not to be late.

items.spanish: Me reprochó que no hubiera llamado.
items.english: She reproached me for not having called.

sections.title: More verbs of the same kind
sections.content: *Señalar* 'to point out', *precisar* 'to specify', *agregar* 'to add' and *recalcar* 'to stress' state a fact too, so they take the indicative: *Señaló que el puente estaba cerrado.* *Agregar* is very common in Latin America for *añadir*.

Ask what the verb is doing. Stating or accepting a fact: indicative. Rejecting a claim, proposing, blaming, or telling someone to do something: subjunctive. *Advertir* and *recordar* are the two that can go either way, depending on whether they inform or give an instruction.
